conviction_note: Findings sum +1.4 (a guide-arithmetic beat-and-raise setup plus a strong Q3 industrial absorption print, partly offset by post-guide share issuance and 5%+ Treasury yields); the scaled number is (2*0.58-1)*3.5 = +0.56, smaller because the beat-and-raise habit is widely known (7/7 up reactions, two raises already), the bar rests on one estimate source plus the company guide, and the stock's 11% slide since July is a rates/dilution story the print does not resolve.
bar: Q3 2026 Core FFO/share ~$1.57-1.58 (Benzinga listed both $1.57 and $1.58; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLD/earnings-forecasts via search snippet, page 403). Cross-check: company FY2026 Core FFO guide $6.22-6.30 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045609/000119312526305416/pld-ex99_2.htm, 2026-07-16) less H1 actual $1.50 (Q1, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045609/000119312526157977/pld-ex99_2.htm) + $1.63 (Q2) = $3.13 implies H2 $3.09-3.17, ~$1.545-1.585 a quarter, so consensus sits at the guide midpoint. Q3 revenue consensus $2,216M (Hudson Labs, 2026-09-28, https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/prologis-q3-2026-earnings-preview-pld-results-and-guidance). FY consensus before the July raise was $6.14-6.17, i.e. likely now ~$6.26-6.28 (not sourced). Bar is company-guide-anchored, single estimate source.
positioning_check: Short interest 18,474,881 shares on 2026-09-30 settlement, ~2.0% of 932.3M shares outstanding, 4.91 days to cover (equibles, FINRA data, https://equibles.com/stocks/pld/shortinterest); up from 15.73M on 2026-08-14 (likely partly Segro merger-arb hedging after the 2026-08-04 firm offer), down slightly from 18.88M on 09-15. Not crowded. Baseline skew_25d +1.97 vol points (mild put premium), put/call OI 0.52 (call-heavy), priced_direction_lean 'balanced'. Run-up: +4.27% over 5 days into the print, -0.75% over 20 days, -11.5% from 52w high; stock was $149.94 on 2026-07-21 and priced a 17.25M-share offering at $139.85 on 2026-08-04; closed $129.84 on 2026-10-01 per a market note. Event-implied move 3.5%, ATM IV 49.2% front expiry.

findings.finding: Prologis's own July guide sets up a mechanical beat-and-raise: FY2026 Core FFO guide $6.22-6.30 minus H1 actual $3.13 ($1.50 Q1 + $1.63 Q2) implies only $1.545-1.585 per quarter in H2, while Q2 Core FFO ex-promote ran at $1.60 and the Q3 consensus is ~$1.57-1.58; the company beat consensus in Q1 ($1.50 vs $1.48) and Q2 ($1.63 vs ~$1.53-1.55) and raised the FY range both times, so a Q3 near the Q2 run-rate (~$1.60) plus a third raise of the range is the base case the guide itself implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: up on 7 of 7 prior prints, median +1.84%; the two 2026 raises bought +1.72% (2026-04-16) and +4.63% (2026-07-16); 2025-10-15 (record leasing, data center) +6.33%; 2026-01-21 +0.25%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at ~$1.57-1.58 sits at the guide midpoint rather than at the Q2 run-rate, i.e. the street models the guide's implied H2 deceleration; if the market priced a third raise the stock would not sit 11.5% below its 52w high with a balanced option lean and analysts' July targets ($150-162) unreached. Partly priced: the beat-and-raise habit is known.
findings.independence: Q1 actual/beat from a separate document: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045609/000119312526157977/pld-ex99_2.htm (2026-04-16). Q2 beat vs $1.53 estimate per Benzinga snippet. Shares the guide document with the development-starts finding.

findings.finding: Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 2026 US industrial report (published 2026-10-09, after Prologis last spoke) shows 76.6 msf of net absorption, the strongest quarter since Q1 2023, 203 msf year to date (strongest nine months since late 2022) and national vacancy down to 6.8%; that YTD pace (~270 msf annualised) runs above Prologis's own July forecast of ~220 msf 2026 US absorption against 195 msf completions, pointing to occupancy at or above the 95.25-95.75% guide and an upgraded market outlook on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Record-leasing/market-tightening prints: 2025-10-15 +6.33%, 2026-07-16 +4.63% (record 67 msf leased). No release-level attribution beyond the coverage cited.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since 10-09 and the 5-day run-up of +4.27% may partly reflect it; it is an industry proxy, so the market cannot know how much Prologis's portfolio or its forecast moves until the call. If fully priced, the stock would have recovered toward the July level rather than sitting ~$17 below it.
findings.independence: Q2 forecast numbers (220 msf absorption vs 195 msf completions) from https://commercialobserver.com/2026/07/prologis-second-quarter-2026-earnings/ (2026-07-16); vacancy 6.8% figure via search summary of https://www.sdcexec.com/warehousing/automation/news/22976132/cushman-wakefield-us-industrial-market-booms-as-vacancy-drops (page 403). Proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: After the July guide, Prologis issued 17.25M new shares (15M + 2.25M greenshoe exercised in full) at $139.85 on 2026-08-05/07, ~$2.4B gross, ~1.85% of shares outstanding, plus a £3.575B term loan, to fund the Segro cash alternative on a deal not expected to close until H1 2027; the July $6.22-6.30 guide did not contain these shares, so the Q4 per-share math carries a drag (partly offset by interest income or debt paydown) that can cap the size of any raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell ~3% on the day the firm offer and the placement were announced (2026-08-04, per tradersunion/freightwaves coverage); no prior print turned on share count.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts likely updated share counts in August, so most is priced; what is not is how management treats the pre-funding in the updated FY range (it lands as a flatter-than-expected raise if not neutralised). What the money buys: a recommended, shareholder-approved acquisition management calls 'largely neutral to minimally dilutive' in year one, so this is a timing drag, not distress.
findings.independence: Term loan and deal terms: https://ir.prologis.com/financials/sec-filings/content/0001104659-26-089980/tm2621154d2_8k.htm (2026-08-04); greenshoe exercise: https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/pld-8-k-2026-08-05-0001104659-26-090724.

findings.finding: The 10-year Treasury hit ~5.22-5.24% in late September 2026, the highest since 2007, which pressures cap rates, fund valuations and strategic-capital promotes (guided at $0 net for the year), contribution/disposition volumes ($2.25-2.75B guide) and development gains, so the call's tone on 2027 and capital deployment is at risk even if leasing is strong.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No release-level history on rates; the stock slid from $149.94 (2026-07-21) to $129.84 (2026-10-01) through the yield rise.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 11.5% drawdown from the high and the late-September slide are the visible imprint. What is not priced is any explicit cut to disposition/contribution or promote assumptions in the updated guide, which only the release reveals. Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company.
findings.independence: October 2026 REIT commentary noting the 10-year rose nearly a full point over six months and an Oct 1 note of PLD -2.09% to $129.84 (search summaries of https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-2144338-20261007 and https://www.money365.market/news/sector/realestate/brief/2026-10-01). Proxy.

findings.finding: Prologis had already started ~$4B of data center projects in 2026 by Q2 (including an $800M, 260-MW build-to-suit), above its prior full-year view, with total development-starts guidance at $4.5-5.5B and a 5.8 GW power pipeline; another raise of development starts or a further data center build-to-suit/sale is a likely positive line on the Q3 release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Data-center-heavy prints: 2025-10-15 +6.33% (record leasing and data center investment), 2026-07-16 +4.63% (dev-starts guide raised $1B at midpoint).
findings.why_not_priced: The data center story is well known; what is not in the price is the size of any Q3 starts/sale, since no Q3 data center announcement surfaced in public searches. Partly priced.
findings.independence: Guide table (dev starts $4.5-5.5B, 5.8 GW pipeline) in the same Q2 supplemental: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045609/000119312526305416/pld-ex99_2.htm (shares a document with the first finding).

findings.finding: Peer First Industrial guided in July that its in-service occupancy would dip to ~93.5% at end of Q3 2026 before recovering to ~95.5% at year end, a reminder that Q3 can show a seasonal/expiry occupancy trough in US industrial portfolios.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No PLD history on peer occupancy; PLD's own period-end occupancy rose 20 bp in Q2 to 95.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer-specific lease-expiry timing, public since July; weak transmission to Prologis, whose guide already covers average occupancy 95.25-95.75%.
findings.independence: none; contradicted in direction by the Cushman national absorption data in the second finding.

outside_window.finding: Segro acquisition: shareholders approved the scheme on 2026-09-28; court sanction, regulatory clearances and completion expected H1 2027; management called it largely neutral to minimally dilutive in year one. Completion and any accretion update are outside the window (call commentary may touch it).

baseline_tension: The findings lean positive with a mild put skew (+1.97) and a balanced priced lean, and a +4.27% 5-day bounce means part of the relief is already taken; the long sits with, not against, the name's 7/7 positive reaction history.
lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the share issuance funds a shareholder-approved acquisition, so it is a timing drag on the guide, not distress; trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): the Cushman absorption proxy trimmed from +0.6 to +0.5; the rates finding trimmed from -0.4 to -0.3 as unconfirmed macro transmission.
Lesson 6 (bar): bar rests on the company guide plus one estimate source that agree, so no hard cap; the Q3 number lands inside the guide and the upside is filed as a guidance finding.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): 7/7 positive reactions, so the beat-and-raise finding kept at +1.2; p_up held at 58, not higher, because the habit is known.
